benchmark_method.wall: Nine fresh processes pinned to CPU 11 per lane. Hyper lanes use 64 timed operations after one warm-up and one preflight; Cavalier uses 65536 timed operations after 128 warm-ups.
benchmark_method.perf: One pinned perf-stat process per artifact and matched disabled control, with 64 timed operations, one warm-up, and one preflight. Counts are control-subtracted and divided by 66.
benchmark_method.allocations: Heaptrack record-only uses eight timed operations, one warm-up, and one preflight. Counts are matched-control-subtracted and divided by ten.
benchmark_method.peak_heap: Valgrind Massif compares one timed prebuilt operation plus preflight with its matched control using exact peak bytes.
benchmark_method.size: Identically configured all-feature and no-default release unit-test executables built in equal-length target directories; actual .text is read from size -A and allocated total from GNU size.
benchmark_method.historical_caveat: Historical mapped construction and end-to-end lanes reject and are not correctness-equivalent throughput controls. Historical direct lanes are correctness-equivalent controls for unrelated drift.
benchmark_method.competitive_caveat: Cavalier Contours 0.7.0 uses binary64 bulge geometry and supplies no selected fields, Hyper policy outcome, retained proof, or guarantee-equivalent regularization. It is throughput context only.

wall_performance.interpretation: The complete optimized exact operation costs 1.989 ms fresh and 1.156 ms prebuilt. Structural source-order reuse removes 15.90% and 19.16% from the first complete implementation. The remaining mapped premium over identical direct exact geometry is about 15%; historical and Cavalier paths do materially less.

deterministic_perf.interpretation: Retired instructions confirm the wall improvement. The optimized prebuilt mapped path uses 11.94M instructions versus 10.20M for identical direct exact geometry; the direct current/historical control is instruction-identical within 0.02%.

allocation_evidence.interpretation: Shared source order removes 30.17% of prebuilt allocation calls and 25.24% of incremental peak heap from the first complete implementation. The optimized nested path is only 9.52% above the direct exact twin in allocation calls and adds no persistent cache or carrier field.

linked_size.interpretation: The all-feature capability plus regression and structural order fast path adds 23,072 actual text bytes. The general overlap-order and forward-range corrections remain useful without predicates and add 9,040 bytes of minimal .text. This is a measured size cost for a 19.16% prebuilt speedup; all persistent object layouts remain unchanged.
